signal_rationale.delta: CAPSTONE completed its extended demonstration phase in 2026 while NASA advanced a two-spacecraft follow-on, delivered navigation hardware for a commercial lunar relay, specified an initial five-satellite relay architecture and opened new lunar infrastructure procurement.
signal_rationale.evidence: The signal combines completed flight demonstration, flight-hardware delivery, contracted follow-on demonstration, service architecture, interoperability standards and current procurement rather than relying on a roadmap alone.
signal_rationale.scale_path: The path runs from autonomous navigation and relays to interoperable multi-provider services, then to persistent surface power, logistics, manufacturing and recurring multi-mission demand.
signal_rationale.transmission: If service infrastructure becomes reliable, mission design can shift from duplicating support capabilities toward buying shared communications, navigation and logistics, changing procurement, industrial organization, workforce needs and access to lunar operations.
signal_rationale.falsifier: Repeated relay delays, failure of multi-provider interoperability, weak non-anchor demand or persistent surface-power/logistics bottlenecks that prevent growth of the lunar installed base would weaken the service-infrastructure thesis.

en.title: Cislunar infrastructure is shifting from mission support toward a service architecture
en.deck: CAPSTONE, commercial lunar relays, LunaNet and new surface-infrastructure procurement show a shift toward reusable cislunar services, while power, logistics and recurring demand remain the binding constraints.
en.regime: Flight-proven navigation demonstrations are converging with commercial relay procurement, interoperability standards and planned service constellations.
en.key_risk: Institutional plans may outpace recurring demand and surface infrastructure, leaving orbital services technically viable but economically dependent on a narrow anchor-customer base.

pt-BR.title: A infraestrutura cislunar está passando de suporte a missões para uma arquitetura de serviços
pt-BR.deck: CAPSTONE, satélites-relé lunares comerciais, LunaNet e novas compras de infraestrutura de superfície mostram migração para serviços cislunares reutilizáveis, enquanto energia, logística e demanda recorrente continuam sendo restrições centrais.
pt-BR.regime: Demonstrações de navegação em voo estão convergindo com contratação de serviços comerciais de retransmissão, padrões de interoperabilidade e constelações planejadas de serviço.
pt-BR.key_risk: Planos institucionais podem avançar mais rápido do que demanda recorrente e infraestrutura de superfície, deixando serviços orbitais tecnicamente viáveis, mas economicamente dependentes de poucos clientes-âncora.
